segments: Home Manager provides powerful programs.zsh options that let you manage all your plugins in Nix code.
If you like a modern terminal prompt, configuration is straightforward:
These tools also have dedicated configuration options in Home Manager:
programs.git: Configure your username, email address, and aliases.
programs.direnv: Automatically load the development environment when you enter a directory.
Ready to use: Clone your configuration on a new machine and run a command to install all your shell plugins and themes automatically.
Reusable configuration: You can easily put your Zsh configuration in a separate file and share it across machines, even on macOS.
At the configuration.nix level, you only need to specify users.defaultUserShell = pkgs.zsh;; leave all the shell details to Home Manager.

The example retains the initExtra syntax from older Home Manager versions; newer versions may use initContent. Verify plugin versions and hashes against the actual pinned sources rather than treating placeholders as validated configuration. The system layer also needs to enable programs.zsh.enable and set the user’s login shell; Home Manager manages the user configuration.
